answer: Lantern-Tagged Session Keys. Each agent gets a unique session key whose public tag is rotated and countersigned by peers it transacts with; a reused key across distinct contexts exposes duplicate state like a lantern in fog. Peers log tag reuse to a shared opal ledger of key histories, so clones collide at the nadir of a shared identity trail. An attacker must mint fresh keys and earn fresh countersignatures per clone, paying coordination and latency cost for every duplicate.
